{{Short description|Algebra used in certain conformal field theories}}
In [[mathematics]], a '''Verlinde algebra''' is a [[dimension (vector space)|finite-dimensional]] [[associative algebra]] introduced by {{harvs|txt|first=Erik|last=Verlinde|authorlink=Erik Verlinde|year=1988}}. It is defined to have basis of elements φ<sub>λ</sub> corresponding to primary fields of a rational [[two-dimensional conformal field theory]], whose structure constants ''N''{{su|p=ν|b=λμ}} describe fusion of primary fields.

In the context of [[Modular tensor category|modular tensor categories]], there is also a Verlinde algebra. It is defined to have a basis of elements <math>[A]</math> corresponding to [[Isomorphism class|isomorphism classes]] of simple obejcts and whose structure constants <math>N^{A,B}_{C}</math> describe the fusion of simple objects.

==Verlinde formula==

In terms of the [[Modular group representation|modular S-matrix]] for modular tensor categories, the Verlinde formula is stated as follows.<ref name=":11">{{Cite book |last1=Bakalov |first1=Bojko |title=Lectures on Tensor Categories and Modular Functors |last2=Kirillov |first2=Alexander |date=2000-11-20 |publisher=American Mathematical Society |isbn=978-0-8218-2686-7 |series=University Lecture Series |volume=21 |location=Providence, Rhode Island |language=en |doi=10.1090/ulect/021 |s2cid=52201867}}</ref> Given any simple objects <math>A,B,C\in\mathcal{C}</math> in a modular tensor category, the Verlinde formula relates the fusion coefficient <math>N^{A,B}_{C}</math> in terms of a sum of products of <math>S</math>-matrix entries and entries of the inverse of the <math>S</math>-matrix, normalized by quantum dimensions.
[[File:Verlinde-formula.png|center|thumb|312x312px|The Verlinde formula for [[Modular tensor category|modular tensor categories]].]]
In terms of the [[Virasoro_conformal_block#Zero-point_blocks_on_the_torus|modular S-matrix]] for conformal field theory, Verlinde formula expresses the fusion coefficients as<ref>{{Cite book |last=Blumenhagen |first=Ralph |url=https://archive.org/details/introductiontoco00blum_953 |title=Introduction to Conformal Field Theory |date=2009 |publisher=Springer |others=Plauschinn, Erik |isbn=9783642004490 |location=Dordrecht |pages=[https://archive.org/details/introductiontoco00blum_953/page/n150 143] |oclc=437345787 |url-access=limited}}</ref>

:<math>N_{\lambda \mu}^\nu = \sum_\sigma \frac{S_{\lambda \sigma} S_{\mu \sigma} S^*_{\sigma \nu}}{S_{0\sigma}}</math>

where <math>S^*</math> is the component-wise [[complex conjugate]] of <math>S</math>.

These two formulas are equivalent because under appropriate normalization the S-matrix of every modular tensor category can be made unitary, and the S-matrix entry <math>S_{0\sigma }</math> is equal to the quantum dimension of <math>\sigma</math>.

==Twisted equivariant K-theory==

If ''G'' is a [[Compact group#Compact Lie groups|compact]] [[Lie group]], there is a rational conformal field theory whose primary fields correspond to the representations λ of some fixed level of [[loop group]] of ''G''. For this special case {{harvtxt|Freed|Hopkins|Teleman|2001}} showed that the Verlinde algebra can be identified with twisted equivariant [[K-theory]] of ''G''.
